question: Who was the founder of the newspaper 'Indian Opinion'? (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Mahatma Gandhi
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahatma Gandhi

Explanation:
The newspaper 'Indian Opinion' was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1903 in South Africa. Its purpose was to raise issues concerning the Indian community in South Africa and spread the idea of non-violent resistance. Through this journal, Gandhi promoted the principles of Satyagraha and non-cooperation. 'Indian Opinion' was initially published weekly in Gujarati, Hindi, Tamil, and English. It served as a crucial medium for Gandhi, later influencing the Indian independence movement. Gandhi remained its editor until 1914, and under his leadership, the paper became the voice of the Indian struggle in South Africa.

question: Where was the ﬁrst session of the Indian National Congress?  (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Madras
Allahabad
Bombay
Calcutta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bombay

Explanation:
The first session of the Indian National Congress (INC) was held on December 28, 1885 at Bombay (now Mumbai) in the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College. The session was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and was attended by 72 delegates. The INC was founded by A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, with the aim of creating a platform for educated Indians to exchange views and cooperate with the British government. The first session primarily discussed political rights, administrative reforms, and Indian participation in civil services. This session is considered the foundation of the Indian national movement.

question: In which of the following cities did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place? (RRB JE ME (31/08/2019) CBT 2)
options: Amritsar
Patiala
Bhatinda
Jalandhar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Amritsar

Explanation:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in the city of Amritsar on 13 April 1919. It was a protest against the Rowlatt Act. British officer General Dyer ordered his troops to fire on unarmed civilians. Hundreds of people were killed in the incident. This event accelerated the Indian independence movement. Rabindranath Tagore returned his knighthood in protest. Udham Singh later assassinated General Dyer as revenge.

question: With which of the following movements is the slogan "Do or Die" associated? (RRB JE (24/05/2019) Shift 1 CBT 1)
options: Swadeshi Movement
Quit India Movement
Civil Disobedience Movement
Non-Cooperation Movement
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Quit India Movement

Explanation:
The slogan "Do or Die" was given by Mahatma Gandhi during the Quit India Movement in 1942. This movement was a major civil disobedience campaign against British rule during World War II. Gandhi ji proclaimed the slogan on August 8, 1942, at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai, inspiring the nation to fight for freedom. The British arrested Congress leaders, but the masses continued the movement without leadership. It is considered the most powerful movement in India's freedom struggle. The Quit India Movement laid the foundation for India's independence in 1947.

question: Who was the first person to observe 'Individual Satyagraha'? (RRB JE (24/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Mahatma Gandhi
Govind Ballabh Pant
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Vinoba Bhave

Explanation:
The Individual Satyagraha was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1940. Its purpose was to demonstrate that the Indian people could offer non-violent resistance against British rule. In this movement, satyagraha was to be observed individually, not collectively. Vinoba Bhave was chosen as the first satyagrahi of this movement. He started his satyagraha on 17 October 1940. Gandhi himself did not observe satyagraha; rather, he led the movement. Vinoba Bhave was a follower of Gandhi and is known for the Bhoodan Movement.

question: Who was the Governor General of India during the Sepoy Mutiny? (RRB JE (26/05/2019) Shift 3 CBT 1)
options: Lord Canning
William Bentinck
Robert Clive
Warren Hastings
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Canning

Explanation:
During the Sepoy Mutiny (1857-1859), the Governor General of India was Lord Canning (1856-1862). The revolt began on 10 May 1857 in Meerut and rapidly spread across northern India. Lord Canning played a crucial role in suppressing the uprising. After the revolt, the Government of India Act 1858 was passed, which ended the rule of the East India Company and placed India directly under the British Crown. Lord Canning subsequently became the first Viceroy of India. His policies brought major administrative changes, including the reorganization of the army and fair treatment of Indians. The event marked a turning point in Indian history, leading to the establishment of the British Raj.

question: India came directly under the rule of the British Crown in the year ______A. 1857B. 1858C. 1859D. 1856 (RRB NTPC Tier I (05/04/2016) Shift 3)

question_hi: 1925 में काकोरी रेल डकैती _______ द्वारा आयोजित की गई थी।A. स्वराज पार्टीB. भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेसC. अनुशीलन समितिD. हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (RRB NTPC Tier I (19/04/2016) Shift 2)
options_hi: A
B
D
C
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन

Explanation:
1925 में काकोरी रेल डकैती को हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HRA) ने अंजाम दिया था। इसका नेतृत्व राम प्रसाद बिस्मिल, अशफाकउल्ला खान और चंद्रशेखर आज़ाद जैसे क्रांतिकारियों ने किया। इस घटना का उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश सरकार के खिलाफ धन प्राप्त करना और क्रांतिकारी गतिविधियों को अंजाम देना था। HRA की स्थापना 1924 में हुई थी और बाद में इसका नाम बदलकर हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HSRA) रखा गया। काकोरी कांड ने भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन को मजबूत किया।
